title: Northgate Credit Cards: One Card per Membership Segment
content:
Northgate member services desk guidance on how many Northgate Credit Cards one person may hold, and when an application is not taken for a membership.

## Rule

1. A person may hold at most one Northgate card linked to a consumer membership and at most one linked to a business membership — so at most 2 Northgate cards in all, one in each segment.
2. An application is not taken for a membership that already has a card whose status is applied, active or restricted.
3. Rewards of a consumer card and a business card are never combined.

## Basis of the judgement in clause 2

- **Which cards count.** Only card accounts linked to the very membership the new card would be linked to. A card linked to the person's other membership is not a card of this membership.
- **What decides.** The card account records — each card's linked membership and its status as the records show it — not the applicant's own description.
- **When.** The records are read before the application is taken.
- **Each application its own record.** Every application is recorded as a separate card account dated with its own application date.

## Status of a card already linked to the same membership

| Status of the existing card on that membership | Effect under clause 2 |
|---|---|
| Applied | The application is not taken |
| Active | The application is not taken |
| Restricted | The application is not taken |
| Declined | Not one of the three statuses; clause 2 does not bar the application |
| Closed | Not one of the three statuses; clause 2 does not bar the application |

## Illustrations (hypothetical members)

- A member's consumer membership has a Northgate Rewards Visa Signature in status active. An application for the Northgate Store Card linked to that same consumer membership is not taken.
- A member's consumer membership has a card whose application is still in status applied. A second application on that membership is not taken while the first stands in status applied.
- A member whose consumer membership has an active card applies for a Northgate Business Store Card linked to their business membership, which has no card. Neither clause 1 nor clause 2 bars it: the new card would be the person's only business-segment card, and its membership has no card at all.
- That member then holds two cards, one per segment. The consumer card's rewards and the business card's rewards are kept on their own accounts and never added together.
